standard_prerequisites.name: The local structure statement for a finite type flat sheaf, and permanence of flatness
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, label proposition-finite-type-flat-at-point (proof line 2690); Morphisms, label morphisms-lemma-flat-permanence (proof line 2695)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first provides an elementary etale neighbourhood and an open subscheme on which the pullback is flat, and the second shows that flatness of the pullback at a point of the fibre implies flatness of the original module there.

core_obligations: Choose the etale neighbourhood and the open subscheme from the local structure statement, noting that the fibre over the new base point agrees with the original fibre because the residue fields agree (proof lines 2686-2691).

Show the neighbourhood is contained in the flat locus: for a point of the intersection the pullback of the module is flat over the new base, so by permanence of flatness the module is flat over the base at that point (proof lines 2692-2695).
Conclude that the flat locus of the fibre is open, since the intersection of the fibre with the open subscheme is an open neighbourhood of each of its points inside it (proof lines 2696-2697).
proof_roadmap: Etale neighbourhood and agreement of the fibres (proof lines 2686-2691).
Flatness of the pullback implies flatness of the module (proof lines 2692-2695).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a locally finite type morphism and a finite type module the set of points of a fibre where the module is flat over the base is open in the fibre (statement lines 2675-2684, tag 05P7-adjacent). The proof uses the local structure statement to produce an etale neighbourhood and an open subscheme on which the pullback is flat, notes that the fibre is unchanged because the residue fields agree, and concludes by permanence of flatness. The reduction to the etale neighbourhood is the substance, so the claim is H2.
